general_summary: DOSE is a collective rooted in the field of architecture that undertakes a proactive and multidisciplinary approach in the exploration of the urban contemporary realm. Working as a think-tank, its practice embraces endogenous and exogenous opportunities for the development of specific projects and non-prescriptive solutions. DOSE acknowledges different cultural sensitivities as important inputs for the construction of speculative and experimental strategies. Moving away from static and hermetic approaches, it promotes the dynamic use of tools and creative processes drawn from its multidisciplinary stance. The outcomes allow for subversion and entertainment as catalysts of stimulus and contamination. DOSE acts in the contemporary urban plays.

CNLL leaded by Nuno Lacerda Lopes, Architect and Lecturer at the faculty of Architecture of the University of Porto develops professional activity in areas as Architecture, Engineering, Design and Scenography . With more than twenty years of exhistence, CNLL reflects the values, methodologies, quality criteria and above all his idea of architecture based on man as the central figure of the built space, in an eternal appeal to the senses and a persistent and irreverent desire for experimentation whilst searching for new materials, forms and concepts of which his works are clear evidence.

general_summary: Nuno Montenegro's office boasts a team that can cater to the full range of technical project planning specialties, from urban planning to the design of public and private developments. The two cornerstones behind its concept are the set of partnerships it has entered into and its drive to foster experimental research. Montenegro's team can provide a design-oriented development concept, the hands-on benefit of a small dynamic company with a well-built network of knowledge connectors, and the technical lead and design expertise of a larger one. In its more than ten years of design practice, the company has earned a reputation for excellence in the master planning and the design of distinctive residential, educational, laboratory facilities, recreational, retail, and mixed-use projects. The approach to projects is collaborative both within the practice itself and in its relationship with clients and consultants, among others. These lines of collaboration are established and maintained right through to the completion of a project, allowing projects, from inception, to be considered holistically - from the aesthetic dimensions to questions regarding the environment, structural integrity, and issues related to cost, program, and value. The office is located near Lisbon, in Portugal, close to the salt marshes of the Tagus River estuary. Silverline is an architecture and construction studio founded in 2008 by Jorge Prata and Eduardo Soares, based in Vila Nova de Gaia. Rooted in the belief that design and execution should form a single, cohesive process, Silverline delivers integrated solutions through a close collaboration between its architecture and construction teams. Each project is approached as a unique response to its physical, social, and cultural context, balancing formal precision with functional clarity and emotional depth. The studio engages contemporary challenges by rethinking ways of living and the dialogue between public and private space. Strategic partnerships — including an ongoing collaboration with Melt81 Studio — enrich Silverline’s design approach, reinforcing its commitment to crafting architectural experiences that are thoughtful, enduring, and human-centered.
